headline: A thousand buttons cycling twelve class strings put eight lanes within 20% of each other, because almost every lookup is a cache hit; the split is between lanes that cache and lanes that recompute regardless.

microbench.why: Roughly twelve distinct class strings serve 1,000 buttons, so most calls hit a cache and the case prices lookup rather than style computation. Eight lanes finish between 1.46M and 1.78M renders/s, led by `next-yak` at 1.78M with each variant condition compiled into a ternary over literal class names. `cnfast` at 1.66M and `stylex` at 1.65M sit in the same band because their merge is a map lookup on repeated keys. The lanes that fall away are the ones that recompute whatever the repetition: `next-yak-nofold` at 744,000 builds a wrapper per instance, `panda` at 768,000 re-resolves its style object, and `emotion` at 368,000 re-serializes from scratch.

autocannon.why: `next-yak` leads at 1,593 req/s with `next-yak-css` at 1,447 and `vanilla` at 1,276. The instructive pair is inside Panda: `panda-recipe` at 893 req/s does 1.6× the work of `panda` at 567 on the same variants, because a recipe resolves its variant table during the build rather than on every call.

attribution.why: Seven lanes total between 0.673 ms and 0.765 ms, which is the floor for 1,000 single-element buttons. `next-yak` books 0.317 ms of lib self-time and still leads on total; `next-yak-css`, `stylex` and `stylex-layers` all record 0.000 ms of lib time and pay about 0.26 ms as component self-time instead. `next-yak-nofold` doubles the total to 1.50 ms on identical source with folding off. `emotion` at 2.87 ms and `goober` at 2.24 ms carry their serializers into every instance.

hydrate.why: Six lanes hydrate between 45.2 ms and 47.2 ms. `next-yak` reads 85.3 ms here, which is the bimodal mode this axis keeps producing on the small cases rather than a property of the lane. `goober` at 89.7 ms and `styled-components` at 91.5 ms sit high in every battery, because both rebuild a sheet before React attaches.

inp.why: Fifteen lanes answer one click between 6.1 ms and 8.1 ms, indistinguishable at this spread. `emotion` at 11.0 ms is the only lane that separates.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Twelve lanes mount between 68.8 ms and 89.0 ms, `next-yak` first at 68.8 ms. Parse and layout dominate and every lane produces the same DOM, so the render ordering compresses. `emotion` at 98.7 ms carries its sheet construction into the mount.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, 0.129 ms to 0.207 ms. Twelve distinct class strings over one element per instance give the engine the same matching work everywhere.

payload.why: `next-yak-css` ships 3,737 gz B against 4,540 B for `next-yak`, the difference being the wrapper runtime. `panda-recipe` at 6,477 B carries 1,442 B of JS, under a third of `panda`'s 4,903 B, because the recipe's variant table is resolved during the build instead of shipped as a resolver. The utility and runtime lanes run from 15.1 kB to 17.0 kB.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: `next-yak` holds 1.96 ms at the largest size while `next-yak-nofold` needs 5.15 ms, a 2.63× gap that widens with the count because the wrapper runs per instance however repetitive the variants are. `emotion` at 12.2 ms sets the far end.
